profile.background: OpenAI CEO (holds no OpenAI equity); former Y Combinator president. His personal fortune (~$6.1B per 2026 estimates) is a venture portfolio held directly and via vehicles including Hydrazine Capital and Apollo Projects, anchored by Helion Energy, Stripe, Retro Biosciences and Oklo. May 2026 court filings gave a rare audited look at his holdings.
profile.focus: The physical substrate of the AI age: fusion (Helion), fission (Oklo), longevity biotech (Retro Biosciences), fintech (Stripe), brain-computer interfaces (Merge Labs, co-founded Aug 2025).
profile.style: Very concentrated, very early, personally enormous checks into moonshots he often chairs or co-founds (reported ~$375M into Helion's 2021 raise, ~$180M into Retro) — then held for a decade-plus; recently unwinding board roles (left Oklo chair Apr 2025, Helion board Mar 2026) to clear OpenAI conflict paths.
profile.thesis: Abundant intelligence requires abundant energy and compute: drive the cost of intelligence and energy toward zero and most other problems become solvable.
profile.latest_investments_summary: Recent moves consolidate the compute-energy-bio triangle around OpenAI: co-founded Merge Labs (brain-computer interface, Aug 2025); Retro Biosciences re-raised in May 2026 at $1.8B (his stake ~$258M per court filings, after a $5B figure circulated in late 2025); Helion remains his largest asset (stake estimates $1.6B-$4.1B) as OpenAI weighs a power supply deal; Oklo stake ~$364M after its 2024 SPAC listing via his AltC vehicle. Pattern: personal capital pre-positions the energy and infrastructure OpenAI will need, with governance separations following.
profile.strategy: From his essay 'Abundant Intelligence': build compute (and the energy behind it) at unprecedented scale so AI capacity never forces triage between curing disease, education, and other goals — 'If we are limited by compute, we'll have to choose which one to prioritize; no one wants to make that choice, so let's go build.'
profile.track_record_note: Personal portfolio; no vehicle publishes returns. Court-disclosed stake values (May 2026) are asset marks, not returns, and net-worth estimates are excluded per methodology.

In June 2026 he left Microsoft's board explicitly to go 'founder mode' on Manas, pursuing 'Move 37'-style AI creativity in chemistry against cancer. profile.strategy: Per his own site: 'current priority is investing in and building with AI to benefit humanity' — he presents himself as 'Entrepreneur. Investor. Strategist.', co-founder of LinkedIn, Inflection and Manas AI and Greylock partner, emphasizing AI development directed at broad human benefit.

profile.background: NVIDIA is the dominant designer of AI accelerator chips and the world's most valuable semiconductor company. Its datacenter GPU franchise has generated enormous cash flow, which it now recycles into the AI ecosystem — by 2026 it had become the single largest corporate equity investor in AI, with more than $40B committed in 2026 alone.
profile.focus: Equity stakes in frontier AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic), neoclouds and datacenter operators (IREN), supply-chain partners (Intel, Corning, Nokia), plus roughly two dozen private AI startup rounds.

profile.strategy: NVIDIA's announced OpenAI partnership commits it to deploy at least 10 gigawatts of NVIDIA systems for OpenAI's next-generation AI infrastructure, with NVIDIA intending to invest up to $100 billion progressively as each gigawatt is deployed — the first gigawatt on the Vera Rubin platform in H2 2026.

profile.background: Treated here as a capital allocator, the US federal government has become one of the largest strategic investors in technology and energy: the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act appropriated $52.7bn (including $39bn of manufacturing incentives), DOE's loan office (renamed the Office of Energy Dominance Financing) holds loan authority exceeding $400bn, and since 2025 Washington has shifted from grants to taking direct equity stakes in strategic companies.
profile.focus: Semiconductor fabrication and advanced packaging (CHIPS incentives), energy and critical-materials supply chains (EDF/LPO loans), and defense-critical inputs — with new direct equity positions in Intel and rare-earth producer MP Materials.
profile.style: Policy-directed capital across grants, loans, loan guarantees, offtake guarantees and, newly, negotiated equity: e.g. converting $8.9bn of unpaid CHIPS grants and Secure Enclave funds into a passive 9.9% Intel common-stock stake, and a DoD preferred-plus-warrants package making the Pentagon MP Materials' largest shareholder with a price floor and 10-year offtake.
profile.thesis: Stated rationale is strategic, not financial: onshoring leading-edge chipmaking, 'restoring America's energy dominance', and securing defense supply chains, with equity stakes framed as ensuring taxpayers share the upside of companies rebuilt with public money.
profile.latest_investments_summary: By 31 Jan 2025 Commerce had finalized $30.7bn of CHIPS grants plus $5.5bn of loans to 19 companies across 40 fab projects. In 2025 the government pivoted to ownership: an $8.9bn / 9.9% Intel stake (Aug 2025, with a 5% warrant tied to foundry control) and the DoD's $400M convertible-preferred investment in MP Materials (Jul 2025). EDF's loan book kept growing to $126.3bn issued plus $36.2bn conditional by mid-2026. The pattern: state capital concentrated on chips, power and critical minerals, increasingly on equity terms.
profile.strategy: Official statements frame the programs as strategic industrial policy: CHIPS incentives to restore US leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing, and the Office of Energy Dominance Financing 'Committed to Restoring America's Energy Dominance', protecting taxpayer interests by monitoring each financed project through construction, completion and operation until loans are repaid.
profile.track_record_note: No return metric exists or is appropriate: the US government is a policy allocator, not a return-seeking fund, and publishes no portfolio performance. Rows above are deployed/committed program capital from Tier-1 sources (CRS, Intel IR, MP Materials IR, energy.gov), flagged as such in notes — they are not AUM in the SWF sense and must not be summed naively (the Intel stake was funded partly from the CHIPS totals).

profile.background: Meta Platforms operates Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, funding one of the largest AI infrastructure programs in history from its advertising cash flow. Capex was $72.2B in 2025 and is guided to $125–145B for 2026; Zuckerberg has pledged more than $600B of US investment by 2028.
profile.focus: Owned AI datacenters (multi-gigawatt campuses such as Hyperion in Louisiana, scalable to 5GW, and Prometheus in Ohio), superintelligence R&D and talent, plus rare large strategic stakes (Scale AI).
profile.style: Predominantly on-balance-sheet capex rather than equity stakes, increasingly paired with novel off-balance-sheet financing — a $27B joint venture with Blue Owl Capital funds Hyperion. When it does buy stakes, they are large and talent-driven (the $14.3B Scale AI deal, June 2025).
profile.thesis: Zuckerberg's stated goal is 'personal superintelligence that helps you achieve your goals,' delivered to billions of people through Meta's platforms — and he argues Meta uniquely has 'the resources and the expertise to build the massive infrastructure required.'

Closed the ~$27B Blue Owl JV for Hyperion (Oct 2025), continued the multi-state datacenter buildout, and digested the $14.3B, 49% Scale AI stake. The pattern: buy compute capacity and elite researchers, not portfolios of startups.
profile.strategy: Meta says it will build 'personal superintelligence for everyone,' bringing it to billions through its products; Zuckerberg writes that Meta has the resources and expertise to build the massive infrastructure required and intends to invest accordingly.

profile.background: Microsoft is one of the world's largest companies, spanning Azure cloud, enterprise software and gaming. It is the largest corporate holder of a frontier AI lab: its cumulative OpenAI investment converted into a stake valued at ~$135B in the October 2025 recapitalization, and it runs one of the biggest AI capex programs on earth (~$175–190B planned for calendar 2026).
profile.focus: Hyperscale AI datacenters (Fairwater-class sites), frontier-lab equity (OpenAI ~27%; Anthropic $5B), and Azure capacity that AI labs contract against ($250B incremental OpenAI commitment; $30B Anthropic commitment).
profile.style: Anchor strategic stakes structured around commercial cloud commitments rather than venture-style portfolios; capital deployed at extreme scale through its own balance sheet and datacenter buildout.
profile.thesis: Microsoft frames its lab investments as securing frontier-model access for Azure: after the OpenAI recapitalization both companies can 'independently continue advancing innovation and growth,' while Microsoft retains exclusive frontier IP rights and a diversified position across labs.
profile.latest_investments_summary: Oct 2025: OpenAI restructuring left Microsoft with ~27% (as-converted, ~$135B) and OpenAI contracted an incremental $250B of Azure. Nov 2025: invested $5B in Anthropic (alongside NVIDIA's ~$10B) as Anthropic agreed to buy $30B of Azure. FY2026 results (Jul 2026) booked a $3.2B gain on Anthropic and a ~$600M markdown on OpenAI; calendar-2026 capex plans ~$175–190B. The pattern: own equity in the labs, and monetize their training demand.
profile.strategy: Microsoft describes the next chapter of the OpenAI partnership as holding ~27% of OpenAI (valued ~$135B) while OpenAI purchases an incremental $250B of Azure services; Microsoft retains frontier-model and IP access and continues building AI infrastructure at global scale.

profile.background: Founder, chairman and CEO of SoftBank Group. profile.focus: Artificial superintelligence (ASI) as a single organizing bet: AI models (OpenAI), semiconductors (Arm, chip ventures), robotics/physical AI, and AI infrastructure (data centers, Stargate).
profile.style: Maximal concentration and personal leverage: 'all in' bets sized in the tens of billions, personal skin-in-the-game via profit-share structures, and multi-decade holding horizons; he says he was 'born to realize' ASI and will work another 10-15 years toward it.
profile.thesis: ASI - AI 10,000x smarter than humans - arrives within a decade; SoftBank should be 'the organiser of the industry in the artificial super intelligence era' across models, chips, robots and infrastructure, targeting NAV of JPY 1,000 trillion by 2042.
profile.latest_investments_summary: The past year is one bet repeated at growing scale: SoftBank completed its $22.5B additional investment in OpenAI on Dec 26, 2025 (after $7.5B via Vision Fund 2 in April 2025), taking aggregate OpenAI ownership to ~11% and total commitments cited at $60-65B. At the June 2026 AGM Son rejected AI-bubble talk as an 'insult,' delayed retirement, and framed a four-front ASI strategy (models, robotics, semiconductors, AI infrastructure). Personal-capital signal: his fortunes, collateralized stock, and reported VF2 profit-share tie him personally to the same trade.
profile.strategy: SoftBank's official announcement of the completed $22.5B OpenAI investment frames the group's strategy as concentrating capital on OpenAI and AI infrastructure toward Son's stated goal of realizing artificial superintelligence; at the 2026 AGM he stated the aim to be the industry's organizer in the ASI era.
profile.track_record_note: No personal vehicle publishes returns. SoftBank Group and Vision Fund performance belong to the corporation (profiled separately), not Son personally; his 17.25% VF2 profit-share is press-reported structure, not a stated return. Net-worth changes excluded per methodology.

profile.background: Former Founders Fund general partner (2008–2024, partner emeritus from Dec 2024) who led bets on SpaceX-era Founders Fund winners including Stemcentrx, Affirm and Oscar Health. In July 2025 he and Quiet Capital co-founder Lee Linden launched GPx, a new ~$500M+ vehicle; press reports Peter Thiel is expected to supply a large share (potentially up to half) of the capital.
profile.focus: US venture: pre-seed/seed exposure via emerging managers, plus direct later-stage (mainly Series B) rounds in those managers' breakout companies.
profile.style: Hybrid model: ~20% of the fund invested as an LP into emerging pre-seed/seed VC funds; ~80% reserved to co-lead later rounds alongside those managers so they can exercise pro-rata or lead without ad-hoc SPVs. Concentrated, founder-quality-driven picking.
profile.thesis: In his own words, venture is 'put the most money into the best companies possible at the best price possible,' with '98%-plus' of any decision based on the strength of the founder; GPx applies that same picking framework to general partners — 'Is there some chance this person could have beaten me in my prime?'
profile.latest_investments_summary: The dominant 2025 move is the GPx launch itself (targeting $500M+, reported first close by Oct 2025) — a bet that the next generation of seed managers, not incumbent mega-funds, will source the best companies, with GPx converting that access into concentrated Series B leads.
profile.strategy: Singerman (Sourcery interview): founder strength drives essentially the whole decision; no portfolio-management dogma ('reserve calculations, and ownership percentages, and all that nonsense'); structural optimism — 'I've actually made a lot of money at betting against the end of the world.'
profile.track_record_note: Neither his Founders Fund vintages nor first-time fund GPx publish returns; GPx is a 2025 first fund with no realized record. No public IRR/TVPI figures found.

profile.background: Amazon runs the world's largest cloud business (AWS) alongside its e-commerce empire, and now operates the largest capital-expenditure budget of any company: 2026 capex guidance was raised to roughly $220B (from ~$200B) in July 2026, overwhelmingly for AI infrastructure.
profile.focus: AI datacenters, networking and custom silicon (Trainium), power capacity, and a concentrated strategic stake in Anthropic — its primary frontier-lab bet.
profile.style: Vertical integration: own datacenters plus in-house chips rather than merchant GPUs where possible; equity deployed in large milestone-structured tranches tied to AWS commercial commitments rather than broad venture portfolios.
profile.thesis: Amazon frames AI as a generational opportunity that justifies building capacity ahead of demand — management said in July 2026 that capacity won't catch up with demand through 2027 — with Trainium economics as the differentiator.
profile.latest_investments_summary: Apr 2026: agreed to invest up to $25B more in Anthropic ($5B immediately, up to $20B tied to commercial milestones) on top of $8B already deployed; in exchange Anthropic committed over $100B of AWS spend across a decade and up to 5GW of Trainium capacity. Project Rainier is live with 500,000+ Trainium2 chips training Claude. Jul 2026: raised 2026 capex to ~$220B citing memory costs. The pattern: fuse the lab stake to captive demand for AWS silicon.
profile.strategy: Amazon's announcement of the expanded Anthropic collaboration describes a $5B investment with up to $20B more tied to milestones, Anthropic committing $100B to AWS over ten years, and up to 5GW of Trainium capacity — deepening AWS as the primary training infrastructure for Claude.

profile.background: Founded in 2009 by Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz on the conviction that 'software would eat the world', a16z has grown into the largest US venture platform, reporting over $100B in assets under management on its own site (as of April 2026). Its registered-investment-advisor structure lets it hold crypto, public stock and other non-traditional venture assets.
profile.focus: Invests from seed through growth across AI, American Dynamism (defense/industry), bio + health, consumer, crypto, enterprise, fintech, games and infrastructure.
profile.style: Full-stack platform firm with large operating teams; leads aggressively at every stage, sizing checks to the magnitude of the potential outcome rather than the absence of weaknesses.
profile.thesis: Software eating the world has become AI eating software: the firm deliberately spreads capital across competing foundation labs, AI infrastructure and AI-native applications, and frames US technological 'dynamism' as a national imperative.
profile.latest_investments_summary: Closed more than $15B across six strategies in 2025 (Growth $6.75B, Apps $1.7B, Infrastructure $1.7B, American Dynamism $1.18B, Bio+Health $700M, other venture ~$3B), and in 2026 committed a further ~$1.7B to AI infrastructure projects on top of its 2024 $1.25B infra fund. Deals run from foundation labs (Mistral, xAI) down to picks-and-shovels bets like Netris's $15M Series A — a pattern of owning every layer of the AI stack, with roughly 40% of new dollars reportedly going to AI.
profile.strategy: a16z describes itself as a platform in 'the relationship business' with a long-term outlook, investing seed-to-growth in technology companies and backing 'the magnitude of the strength of the idea and the team, not ... their lack of weaknesses', across AI, bio, crypto, enterprise, fintech and American Dynamism.
profile.track_record_note: Private partnership; a16z does not publicly disclose fund IRR/TVPI. The only public performance data (leaked internal figures reported in 2019, and Cambridge Associates quartile rankings of its 2016 funds) predates the FY2021-2025 target window, so no rows are recorded.

profile.background: DigitalBridge Group (NYSE: DBRG, ~$2.9bn market cap; formerly Colony Capital) is the dedicated digital-infrastructure alternative asset manager led by Marc Ganzi, with $119bn AUM (Mar 31, 2026) across 45+ portfolio companies. In December 2025 SoftBank Group agreed to acquire DigitalBridge for $4bn (stockholders approved April 2026) to scale next-generation AI infrastructure.
profile.focus: Pure-play digital infrastructure across five verticals: data centers, macro cell towers, fiber, small cells and edge infrastructure, plus digital credit, liquid and venture strategies; global (US, Europe, Japan, LatAm).
profile.style: Control equity in scaled platforms alongside co-investors, run by a 'full stack' invest-operate-capitalize model; multi-billion platform deals funded through its DigitalBridge Partners flagship series ($11.7bn total commitments for DBP III including co-invest).
profile.thesis: DigitalBridge calls itself 'the Infrastructure Partner to the Digital Economy,' arguing AI and cloud create $400bn+ of annual global capex that specialist owner-operators are best placed to capture.
profile.latest_investments_summary: A rapid-fire platform build-out amid its own sale to SoftBank: DBP III closed at $11.7bn (Nov 2025); take-private of broadband operator WideOpenWest with Crestview (Dec 2025); completed Yondr Group hyperscale developer acquisition with La Caisse (Jul 2025); acquired NEC's data center assets with JEXI (Mar 2026) and launched the Nippon Gateway Infrastructure platform in Japan (Jul 2026); agreed a strategic combination with ArcLight (May 2026) to sit at the convergence of power, AI and digital infrastructure.
profile.strategy: From its site: DigitalBridge invests across 'five key digital infrastructure verticals: data centers, macro cell towers, fiber networks, small cells, and edge infrastructure' with a "'full stack' approach" pairing capital with the right risk profiles across $400bn+ of annual digital capex, as 'the Infrastructure Partner to the Digital Economy.'
profile.track_record_note: DigitalBridge does not publicly disclose fund-level net IRRs/TVPI for the DigitalBridge Partners series in citable sources, so only stock-return rows are included.

profile.background: Co-founder of Sun Microsystems and former Kleiner Perkins GP who founded Khosla Ventures in 2004 — initially deploying largely his own capital before taking outside LPs. Ranked No. 1 on the 2026 Forbes Midas List; KV was the first venture firm into OpenAI ($50M initial commitment, 2019). His personal balance sheet and the firm are deeply intertwined, with the personal angel portfolio (~15 companies on trackers) small relative to KV.
profile.focus: High-risk 'science experiment' deep tech: AI, fusion/nuclear, robotics, healthcare, climate and infrastructure reinvention.
profile.style: Bold, contrarian, failure-tolerant concentrated bets with long horizons; hands-on 'venture assistance' to founders; willing to fund pre-commercial science others won't.
profile.thesis: Technology can 'reinvent societal infrastructure' and make expertise — doctors, tutors, professional services — effectively free through AI; transformative goals are reached incrementally ('Nobody ever got to Mount Everest without getting to base camp first').
profile.latest_investments_summary: Personal-vehicle deal flow is sparse and mostly historical (trackers' latest distinct personal row: Basis, Series A, Dec 2024); his capital now overwhelmingly deploys through Khosla Ventures — Fund XIII closed at $3.5B in 2024 with mandates around fusion, humanoid robots and AI infrastructure, and KV was among the most active US AI investors through 2025–2026.
profile.strategy: KV's official page: reinventing societal infrastructure with technology; targeting societally critical, underserved sectors (biotech, transit, cybersecurity, quantum, AI) where technology platforms can extend resource-rich lifestyles globally.
profile.track_record_note: Khosla Ventures does not publicly disclose fund IRR/TVPI, and no LP disclosures for recent vintages were found; his personal angel returns are unpublished. Forbes net-worth estimates are not returns and are excluded.

profile.background: Netscape co-founder and co-founder/general partner of Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), now ~$90B+ AUM and among the world's largest venture firms. His personal angel track (with Ben Horowitz) predates a16z; today most of his capital deploys through the firm, with occasional direct personal checks.
profile.focus: Software and AI platforms; personal checks recently in AI simulation/analytics (Electric Twin, Macroscope) plus 'American dynamism'-adjacent themes; he also directs large personal sums to AI-policy political vehicles (Leading the Future), which are not investments.
profile.style: Personally low-volume (a handful of named direct deals; most recent: Electric Twin Series A, Sep 2025) — the real allocation engine is a16z, where he sets an aggressive, platform-scale, full-stack venture model.
profile.thesis: Techno-optimism: technological progress through free markets is the engine of human flourishing — 'technology is the glory of human ambition and achievement, the spearhead of progress' — so accelerate building rather than restrain it.
profile.latest_investments_summary: Personal direct activity in the last 12 months is thin and AI-flavored: an Electric Twin Series A participation (Sep 2025) and Macroscope, in productivity/simulation software. The larger personal-capital story is political-adjacent: heavy funding of the Leading the Future super-PAC to shape AI regulation (spending, not capital allocation, so excluded from events). Substantive dealflow continues through a16z rather than his own balance sheet.
profile.strategy: His authored Techno-Optimist Manifesto: markets plus technology drive abundance; society should deliberately accelerate innovation — pessimism and precaution are the enemy; 'technology is the glory of human ambition and achievement, the spearhead of progress.'
profile.track_record_note: No personal vehicle publishes returns; a16z fund performance is confidential to LPs and belongs to the firm, not Andreessen personally. No source states a personal return, so none is recorded.

profile.background: Co-founder and CEO of Figma; Thiel Fellow who took the company public on the NYSE in July 2025 in one of the largest tech IPO debuts (reported ~$68B day-one valuation; his ~9% stake valued around $6.6B by Forbes). In parallel he is one of the more prolific operator-angels of his generation, with 118 personal investments per PitchBook.
profile.focus: Seed through Series B in AI, developer tools, design/media and content, enterprise software, fintech and web3.
profile.style: Small operator-angel checks — reported $10K–$500K range — as a participant, not a lead; picks driven by product taste and founder quality rather than a portfolio-construction model.
profile.thesis: No formally published personal thesis; his public statements center on AI radically expanding who can create and design, with taste and craft becoming the differentiator — the lens visible in his angel picks.
profile.latest_investments_summary: Recent personal deals: Arcadia Medicine (drug discovery), PlayerZero (software analytics) and Huxe (productivity) in 2025, and Revel (business/productivity software, May 2026) — small checks clustered around AI-native tools and creation/analysis workflows, continuing post-IPO.
profile.strategy: In his 2026 Stratechery interview he lays out the worldview behind his bets: AI collapses the cost of producing software and design, shifting value to taste, craft and multiplayer-native product experiences.
profile.track_record_note: Individual angel; no published returns for his personal portfolio. His Figma stake's IPO value is founder equity, not an allocation return, and is excluded.

profile.background: New York venture firm founded by Josh Kushner in 2010. Built a record of repeat-conviction bets on generational private companies — OpenAI, Stripe, SpaceX — and closed its largest-ever fund, the $10B Thrive Capital Partners X, in February 2026 after heavy oversubscription. Also incubates companies directly.
profile.focus: Internet, software and technology-enabled companies, with current weight on growth-stage AI leaders; US-centric.
profile.style: Deliberately concentrated: fewer, larger positions than peer funds, doubling into the same companies repeatedly (it backed OpenAI four separate times at four different valuations) and building via incubations as well as investing.
profile.thesis: Back a very small number of companies believed capable of defining their era, and keep compounding capital into them as conviction grows rather than diversifying broadly.
profile.latest_investments_summary: Invested roughly $1B in OpenAI at a $285B valuation in December 2025 (CNBC) and was expected to participate in OpenAI's subsequent ~$100B+ raise; closed the $10B Fund X in February 2026; also a repeat investor in Anysphere (Cursor) before its $60B SpaceX acquisition. The pattern: ever-larger, ever-more-concentrated checks into perceived AI winners it already knows.
profile.strategy: Thrive's own description is spare: it 'builds and invests in internet, software, and technology-enabled companies', operating both an investing arm and an incubations program.
profile.track_record_note: Private firm; fund IRR/TVPI are not publicly disclosed and no LP/endowment disclosures covering FY2021-2025 were found. Press describes 'outsized success' of its OpenAI/SpaceX/Stripe positions but reports no verifiable return figures.

profile.background: BlackRock (NYSE: BLK, ~$176bn market cap) is the world's largest asset manager, hitting a record $15.3 trillion AUM in Q2 2026 after $868bn of net inflows over twelve months. Founded 1988 by Larry Fink, it has transformed from an index/ETF giant (iShares crossed $6 trillion) into a combined public-markets, private-markets and technology platform via the GIP, HPS and Preqin acquisitions.
profile.focus: Everything from index/ETFs and active strategies to fast-growing private markets - infrastructure (GIP), private credit (HPS) - plus the Aladdin technology business; its capital-deployment edge is now concentrated in AI infrastructure and energy.
profile.style: Platform scale and consortium deal-making: multi-tens-of-billions infrastructure vehicles and partnerships (AI Infrastructure Partnership with Microsoft, MGX and Nvidia) rather than single-company venture bets; targets $400bn of private-markets fundraising by 2030.
profile.thesis: Fink: 'BlackRock is simultaneously a leading public markets manager, a scaled private markets platform, and a global technology company' - with client portfolios steered toward infrastructure, AI and retirement assets as the growth engines.
profile.latest_investments_summary: The pattern is mega-scale AI infrastructure via consortiums: the AI Infrastructure Partnership (with MGX, Microsoft, Nvidia) agreed in Oct 2025 to acquire Aligned Data Centers for ~$40bn - the largest data center deal ever and AIP's first investment toward $30bn of equity ($100bn+ with debt), closing H1 2026; GIP closed its fifth flagship at $25.2bn (largest private infra fund raise); GIP+HPS arranged multibillion-dollar debt financing for Meta's AI data centers; and GIP formed a ~€2bn data center JV with ACS.
profile.strategy: BlackRock describes itself (Q2 2026 earnings release) as 'simultaneously a leading public markets manager, a scaled private markets platform, and a global technology company,' with record inflows driven by ETFs, private markets, active fixed income and Aladdin technology services.
profile.track_record_note: BlackRock reports AUM and net flows rather than a firm-level fund return composite (client returns accrue across thousands of index/active funds), so only stock-return rows are included.

profile.background: San Francisco firm founded in 2005 by Peter Thiel with PayPal co-founders; early backer of SpaceX, Palantir, Facebook and Anduril. In May 2026 it closed its largest-ever vehicle, a $6B growth fund — $4.5B from LPs including sovereign wealth funds and $1.5B from Thiel and other partners/employees.
profile.focus: Transformative 'hard' technology: AI, defense, aerospace, fintech and bio, from seed through very large late-stage positions.
profile.style: Highly concentrated and contrarian — the new $6B fund is expected to deploy over two to three years across roughly a dozen companies; famously founder-aligned, letting portfolio achievements rather than firm marketing speak.
profile.thesis: Fund civilization-scale technology that consensus finds heretical: 'progress is a history of persecuted weirdos', existential-scale risk is inseparable from genuine progress, and the interesting question is 'What would you build if you could start over?'
profile.latest_investments_summary: Closed the $6B growth fund (May 2026) aimed at late-stage AI, defense and fintech; its prior fund put $1.25B into Anthropic at a $350B valuation and $1B into Anduril. The pattern is doubling down with billion-dollar checks on already-scaled winners at the intersection of AI and national security.
profile.strategy: Founders Fund presents itself through its portfolio (Anduril, SpaceX, Palantir) and its manifesto pages: it champions dissent and 'dangerous' ideas, rejects both techno-pessimism and uncritical optimism, and backs founders reimagining entire industries — 'What would you build if you could start over?'
profile.track_record_note: Private partnership; fund IRR/TVPI not publicly disclosed. Press-reported performance of early vintages (e.g. its 2007/2011 funds) predates the FY2021-2025 target window, so no rows are recorded.

profile.background: The archetypal solo mega-angel: ex-Google and Twitter executive, co-founder of Color Genomics and Mixer Labs (acquired by Twitter), turned one-person venture franchise. Raised over $1B for his third solo vehicle in 2021, and in mid-2025 was reported raising a new solo fund of roughly $1.5B with the target later reported around $3B — institutional scale with no partnership.
profile.focus: AI-first across stages — foundation models, AI applications, infrastructure — plus defense, fintech, dev tools and longevity/bio; predominantly US.
profile.style: Solo GP writing checks from seed to growth across a very large portfolio; low-process, network- and judgment-driven, able to move faster than committee-based firms; multi-stage investing via his Gil&Co vehicles.
profile.thesis: Self-described 'technology entrepreneur, investor, & future forward optimist' focused on major technology shifts; currently argues AI's early winners are now visible and that AI applied to traditional businesses (including roll-ups) is the next big opportunity.
profile.latest_investments_summary: Last ~12 months: doubling down on the AI stack where he was early (Perplexity, Harvey, Character, Mistral, Anthropic/OpenAI exposure, Abridge, Braintrust, Decagon, Cognition) while pushing a new theme of AI-powered roll-ups of services businesses (per TechCrunch, June 2025), backed by the new multi-billion-dollar solo fund raise.
profile.strategy: From his own site: a series of investments, incubations and operating companies oriented at 'the technology future' — early generative-AI positioning, longevity/bio interests, and multi-stage venture investing through Gil&Co.
profile.track_record_note: Solo VC; fund IRR/TVPI never publicly reported and no LP disclosures found. Reported fund sizes ($1B+ in 2021; ~$1.5–3B raise reported 2025) are capital raised, not returns.

profile.background: Anthropic is the AI safety company behind the Claude models, founded in 2021 and valued at ~$350B after Google's April 2026 investment. Tracked here as a corporate allocator: historically capital-light and cloud-dependent, it began deploying its own capital into physical infrastructure in late 2025.
profile.focus: Compute infrastructure: custom-built US datacenters (with GPU-cloud partner Fluidstack), plus enormous multi-year compute commitments across three clouds and three chip platforms — AWS/Trainium, Google/TPU, and Azure/NVIDIA.
profile.style: Deliberately multi-vendor and commitment-driven: rather than equity investing, it commits tens of billions in purchase obligations tied to its investors' platforms, and now direct capex via partner-built dedicated sites.
profile.thesis: Anthropic says the scale of its infrastructure investment is necessary to meet growing demand for Claude from hundreds of thousands of businesses while keeping its research at the frontier, and frames the US buildout as supporting American AI leadership.
profile.latest_investments_summary: Nov 2025: announced a $50B American AI infrastructure program with Fluidstack, starting with custom datacenters in Texas and New York (online through 2026, ~800 permanent jobs), and agreed to purchase $30B of Azure compute alongside the Microsoft/NVIDIA investments. Oct 2025: expanded Google Cloud deal for up to 1M TPUs. Apr 2026: committed $100B of AWS spend over a decade with up to 5GW of Trainium. Jul 2026: Nexus Data Centers in talks for $15B financing for an Anthropic campus in Texas, with Google as a guarantor structure emerging.
profile.strategy: Anthropic's announcement describes a $50B investment in American computing infrastructure — custom datacenters built with Fluidstack in Texas and New York with more sites to come — sized to meet demand for Claude and to keep its frontier research capability, aligned with US AI-leadership goals.
profile.track_record_note: Private company: no listed stock, so no stock_total_return_pct series exists, and Anthropic does not publicly disclose fund-style returns or financial statements. Reported valuation marks (e.g. ~$183B in Sep 2025 to ~$350B in Apr 2026 per press reports) are financing valuations, not returns, and are therefore not recorded as track-record rows.

profile.background: MGX is an Abu Dhabi technology investment company established in March 2024 under the emirate's Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council, with Mubadala and AI group G42 as foundational partners and Sheikh Tahnoun bin Zayed as chairman. Press reports describe a ~$100bn target platform; in July 2026 it closed a $49bn AI fund, one of the largest sector-focused vehicles ever raised.
profile.focus: Three stated areas: AI infrastructure (data centers and connectivity), semiconductors (logic and memory design and manufacturing), and AI core technologies and applications (models, software, data, life sciences, robotics), in the UAE and globally.
profile.style: Very large anchor checks deployed fast, usually alongside mega-consortia (Stargate with OpenAI/SoftBank/Oracle; AI Infrastructure Partnership with BlackRock's GIP and Microsoft) — pairing direct stakes in frontier labs with control-scale infrastructure deals.
profile.thesis: CEO Ahmed Yahia frames the mission as ensuring Abu Dhabi and the UAE are 'not just observers of the AI revolution, but active participants and beneficiaries of the most transformative technology of our time', with an emphasis on responsible, inclusive AI.
profile.latest_investments_summary: Founding equity partner in the $500bn Stargate AI-infrastructure venture (~$7bn planned contribution); invested in OpenAI's 2025 primary round at a $300bn valuation and bought further shares in the $6.6bn secondary at a $500bn valuation; a significant backer of Anthropic; joined the AIIP/GIP consortium's ~$40bn acquisition of Aligned Data Centers (Oct 2025); closed a $49bn AI fund in July 2026. The pattern: own both the frontier labs and the compute layer beneath them.
profile.strategy: MGX says it will 'invest to accelerate the development and adoption of AI and advanced technologies through world-leading partnerships both in the UAE and globally', to 'enable the advancement and deployment of leading edge technologies intended to improve the lives of current and future generations', across AI infrastructure, semiconductors, and AI core technologies and applications.
profile.track_record_note: Founded March 2024; a private state-backed vehicle that has published no audited returns and no official AUM. The ~$100bn platform size and $49bn fund close are press-reported fundraising figures, not performance. No source states a return, so no rows — this is honest, not missing coverage.

profile.background: SoftBank Group is Masayoshi Son's Tokyo-listed technology investment holding company (TSE: 9984; ~$200bn market cap after a 2025 AI-driven re-rating). It spans the Vision Funds (SVF1 $100bn, SVF2), a ~90% stake in Arm, telecom roots, and a rapidly growing AI-infrastructure arm including the Stargate program with OpenAI and Oracle.
profile.focus: AI across the whole stack: foundation models (OpenAI), semiconductors (Arm, Ampere), robotics, and AI data center / power infrastructure; global, with the largest bets in the US.
profile.style: Extremely concentrated, conviction-driven mega-checks (tens of billions into single names), often taking control or anchor positions; tolerant of leverage at the holding-company level; buys entire platforms when conviction is high.
profile.thesis: Son's stated worldview: the 'Information Revolution' is entering an AI phase that will bring 'greater innovation and disruption than the past 300 years,' and SoftBank positions itself as a 'Vision Capitalist' organizing capital toward artificial super intelligence.
profile.latest_investments_summary: The last 12 months are a single-minded ASI land-grab: a definitive agreement (Feb 2026) for a $30bn follow-on into OpenAI via Vision Fund 2 at a $730bn pre-money, in $10bn tranches in April, July and October 2026 (cumulative OpenAI investment to reach $64.6bn); the $500bn Stargate data center JV with OpenAI and Oracle; and a $4bn agreement (Dec 2025, shareholder-approved Apr 2026) to acquire DigitalBridge, adding ~$119bn of digital-infrastructure AUM. FY2025 (ended Mar 2026) Vision Fund gains of ~$46bn were driven almost entirely by OpenAI (fair value $79.6bn vs $34.6bn cost).
profile.strategy: SoftBank's stated philosophy is 'Information Revolution - Happiness for everyone,' with a 300-year vision; it describes itself as investing in companies leveraging AI to drive human progress, arguing the AI revolution will exceed the disruption of the past 300 years.
profile.track_record_note: SoftBank reports Vision Fund performance as absolute segment investment gains/losses (e.g. ~$46bn gain in FY2025 ended Mar 2026, OpenAI fair value $79.6bn vs $34.6bn cost), not as fund net IRR or TVPI in its summary reporting, so no fund_irr/tvpi rows are included. Stock rows are the USD ADR; JPY-denominated returns on TSE:9984 differ due to FX.
