Brookfield agreed in July 2026 to acquire it from Blackstone Energy Transition Partners at a ~$7B enterprise value (~$3B equity).

nodes.label: AirTrunk SYD3 (Western Sydney)
nodes.description: 400+MW hyperscale data center in Kemps Creek, Western Sydney, operated by Blackstone-owned AirTrunk — billed as Asia-Pacific's largest by capacity and the first phase of a larger campus; Blackstone finalized a ~A$4.3B (US$3B) five-year syndicated construction loan for the project in July 2026.

nodes.label: Databricks
nodes.description: Data and AI platform company (the 'lakehouse') founded by the creators of Apache Spark and led by Ali Ghodsi. In July 2026 it announced a ~$3B strategic round led by existing investor Coatue at a $188B valuation — its second raise of 2026, up 40% from the $134B mark set in February.

nodes.label: Oaktree Capital Management
nodes.description: Los Angeles-based alternative asset manager co-founded in 1995 by Howard Marks and Bruce Karsh, best known for credit and distressed-debt investing. Brookfield, a partner since 2019, completed acquisition of the remaining ~26% it did not own for ~$3.0B on July 31, 2026, taking 100% ownership and forming a ~$365B combined credit platform.

nodes.label: Microsoft Frontier Company
nodes.description: New Microsoft operating unit for enterprise AI transformation, backed by a $2.5B commitment and 6,000 industry and engineering experts embedded inside customer organizations to design, deploy and improve AI systems at scale. Led by president Rodrigo Kede Lima; early engagements include LSEG, Unilever, Land O'Lakes and Novo Nordisk.

nodes.label: Meta-BlackRock El Paso data center venture
nodes.id: target:Meta-BlackRock El Paso data center venture
nodes.description: Joint venture announced July 2026 to develop a ~$14B, 1 GW AI data-center campus in El Paso, Texas: BlackRock-managed funds own 80% (contributing ~$4.9B cash, partly funded by a $12.5B debt financing) and Meta 20% (contributing land and construction-in-progress valued at ~$2.3B). Meta manages construction and will be sole initial occupant; capacity comes online from 2028.

nodes.label: Nebius Group N.V.
nodes.description: Amsterdam-headquartered, Nasdaq-listed AI cloud ('neocloud') provider that emerged from the former Yandex N.V. NVIDIA invested $2B via pre-funded warrants in a March 2026 private placement — a ~9.3% stake disclosed in a July 13D filing — alongside a partnership targeting more than 5GW of NVIDIA-powered AI capacity by 2030.

nodes.label: Thrive Holdings
nodes.description: Holding company launched in 2025 by Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital that acquires controlling stakes in traditional services businesses (initially accounting and IT services) and rebuilds their operations around AI; OpenAI holds an ownership stake. Raised roughly $2B in July 2026 from SoftBank, Altimeter and D1 Capital, following an earlier $1B from Thrive-affiliated institutions.

nodes.label: Lancium
nodes.description: Power-infrastructure developer behind the 1,000-acre Lancium Clean Campus in Abilene, Texas — the first operational site of the Stargate AI data-center initiative (SoftBank/OpenAI/Oracle). Backed by Blackstone; NVIDIA is reported to be investing $2B for roughly 20% (up to $3B total) at a ~$10B valuation, with a possible 2027 IPO.

nodes.label: Blue Origin
nodes.description: Jeff Bezos's space company (founded 2000): New Glenn heavy-lift rockets, BE-4 engines, the Blue Moon lunar lander and New Shepard suborbital flights. In July 2026 it raised its first-ever outside round — about $10B at a $130B valuation — with Bezos putting in $2B alongside ~$4B from Coatue; Bezos had previously funded it with roughly $30B.

nodes.label: Firmus
nodes.description: Sydney-based AI infrastructure company building Nvidia-architecture 'AI factories' with proprietary immersion-cooling and grid-aware technology across Australia and Asia-Pacific (Project Southgate rollout, Indonesia next). Raised a fully subscribed $2B strategic equity round from Blackstone, Coatue, Nvidia and Jane Street at a post-money valuation above $10.5B.

nodes.label: ABB Robotics
nodes.description: Industrial-robotics division of Swiss engineering group ABB, one of the world's largest industrial robot makers, being acquired by SoftBank Group for $5.4B (announced October 2025, closing expected mid-to-late 2026) as part of SoftBank's AI-plus-robotics push; banks wrapped a $1.75B-equivalent acquisition loan in July 2026.

nodes.label: ABB Robotics acquisition financing
nodes.description: A $1.75B-equivalent syndicated loan package (USD and EUR term loans from a four-bank group) backing SoftBank's $5.375B acquisition of ABB's industrial robotics division — a ~7,000-employee business with $2.3B of 2024 revenue that SoftBank is buying as part of its 'Physical AI' push; the deal is expected to close mid-to-late 2026.

nodes.label: Atoms
nodes.description: Industrial-AI company from Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick (rebranded from City Storage Systems, the CloudKitchens parent), building software, sensors, robotics and AI to automate whole industrial sectors — food production, mining, construction and heavy transport. Raised $1.7B led by a16z, with Ben Horowitz joining the board and Uber, Bain Capital Ventures and Fifth Wall participating.

nodes.label: Sila Nanotechnologies
nodes.description: Alameda, CA battery-materials company (founded 2011 by ex-Tesla engineer Gene Berdichevsky) making silicon-carbon anodes at its Moses Lake, WA plant. Received a conditional loan commitment of up to $1.4B from the Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital to expand anode capacity and build a lithium-ion cell facility for defense supply chains (satellites, UAS, munitions).

nodes.label: SK-KKR Korea renewable energy platform
nodes.description: South Korea's largest renewable energy platform, a 2 trillion won (~$1.3B) venture launched by SK Inc. and KKR in mid-2026, consolidating wind, solar and fuel-cell assets from SK affiliates (SK Innovation, SK ecoplant, SK eternix) — 1.7 GW operating with a pipeline toward 10 GW. KKR (via its Asia Pacific infrastructure strategy) holds management control; the platform targets clean-power demand from AI data centers and chip fabs.

nodes.label: NAVER Corporation
nodes.description: South Korea's dominant internet company (search, commerce, cloud), now building sovereign AI infrastructure. In July 2026 NVIDIA announced a planned $1B investment for a ~4.5% stake, alongside up to $9B of Brookfield funding, to expand NAVER's NVIDIA DSX AI factory at its GAK Sejong data center from 55 MW to 200 MW by 2028, with a stated path to 1 GW.

nodes.label: U.S. semiconductor fabrication facility (unnamed)
nodes.description: Unnamed U.S. chip fab receiving a $1.0B incremental construction funding from Brookfield in Q2 2026, per Brookfield Asset Management's results release. Brookfield's flagship fab exposure is its semiconductor co-investment partnership with Intel (up to $15B for 49% of Intel's Arizona fab expansion), with which this funding is consistent, though the release does not name the facility.

nodes.label: Valar Atomics
nodes.description: Nuclear startup building standardized small modular reactors through vertically integrated manufacturing, targeting power for AI, industry and national security. Its Ward 250 reactor reached self-sustaining criticality in June 2026 — the first reactor taken critical outside a national lab by a company. Raised a $1B Series B led by Sequoia, plus a $200M credit facility from Erebor Bank and J.P. Morgan.

nodes.label: Lucid Group
nodes.description: US luxury electric-vehicle maker (Air sedan, Gravity SUV) majority-owned by Saudi Arabia's PIF; on 2026-07-06 it drew $800M from delayed-draw term loan facilities provided by PIF affiliate Ayar Third Investment, its second 2026 draw, lifting pro-forma liquidity to about $4.7B after a Q2 delivery miss.

nodes.label: Chai Discovery
nodes.description: San Francisco AI-for-drug-discovery company (founded 2024 by Joshua Meier, Jack Dent, Matthew McPartlon and Jacques Boitreaud) building foundation models that predict and reprogram molecular interactions for pre-clinical drug design. Raised a $400M Series C at a $3.8B valuation led by Index Ventures with Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia and Dimension; has collaborations with Eli Lilly and Pfizer.

nodes.label: Coatue Growth Fund VI Private Investors US, LLC
nodes.id: target:Coatue Growth Fund VI Private Investors US, LLC
nodes.description: Delaware feeder vehicle (Form D filed July 2026, administered by J.P. Morgan Private Investments) that channels J.P. Morgan private clients into Coatue Growth Fund VI, Coatue Management's sixth growth-stage venture fund. The filing reports $778.23M sold in an indefinite offering, with first sale July 2, 2026.

nodes.label: DigitalBridge Credit II
nodes.description: Second vintage of DigitalBridge's digital-infrastructure credit fund series, lending (first-lien, second-lien and junior debt) to data center, fiber, tower and related digital infrastructure companies; managed from Boca Raton by the firm led by Marc Ganzi. A July 2026 Form D amendment reports $711.4M sold across its onshore, offshore, Ontario and Luxembourg parallel vehicles.

nodes.label: Mariana Minerals
nodes.description: San Francisco software-first critical-minerals company (CEO Turner Caldwell) that engineers, builds and operates mines and refineries on its MarianaOS platform; flagship sites include Copper One in southeastern Utah and Lithium One in East Texas. Raised a $310M Series B led by Khosla Ventures with a16z, Breakthrough Energy, BHP Ventures and In-Q-Tel — ~$400M raised to date.

nodes.label: Etched
nodes.description: AI inference hardware company founded by Gavin Uberti and Rob Wachen, building rack-scale inference clusters (with technologies like Low Voltage Inference and Cluster Scale Memory) after starting with its transformer-specialized Sohu chip. Raised a $300M Series C led by Sequoia at a $10.3B valuation in July 2026, with a16z, Jane Street and SK Hynix; over $1B raised in total.

nodes.label: Greenoaks Prime Radiant Founders LP
nodes.description: A code-named Greenoaks deal vehicle: a Delaware LP formed in 2026 and renamed from 'Greenoaks Generations Founders LP' per its amended Form D, which reports $576.5M raised from 11 investors (first sale June 26, 2026). Promoters are Greenoaks partners Neil Mehta and Benjamin Peretz; the underlying deal target is undisclosed.

nodes.label: Whatnot
nodes.description: Live-shopping marketplace (founded 2019, CEO Grant LaFontaine) where sellers broadcast live shows to sell collectibles, fashion and more. Closed a $545M Series G at a $20B valuation — roughly double its Oct 2025 mark — led by ICONIQ, Lightspeed and Avra, with returning backers including Andreessen Horowitz, DST Global and CapitalG; ~$1.5B raised to date.

nodes.label: Coatue Growth Fund VI Private Investors Cayman, L.P.
nodes.id: target:Coatue Growth Fund VI Private Investors Cayman, L.P.
nodes.description: Cayman-domiciled feeder vehicle for Coatue Growth Fund VI, Coatue Management's sixth growth-stage fund targeting late-stage technology and AI companies; a Form D filed 2026-07-15 reported roughly $527M raised into this offshore vehicle (a parallel US feeder reported ~$778M).

nodes.label: Gravis Robotics AG
nodes.description: Zurich-based autonomy company (2022 ETH Zurich spinout, founded by Ryan Luke Johns, Dominic Jud, Marco Tranzatto and Burak Cizmeci) whose hardware and software let excavators and other earthmoving equipment operate autonomously. SoftBank is weighing building a substantial stake via a new holding company (Roze) through staged share purchases and capital injections at a valuation above $500M; the startup previously raised $23M.

nodes.label: Sunrise Energy Metals
nodes.description: ASX-listed critical-minerals developer (SRL, Melbourne; backed by Robert Friedland) behind the 100%-owned Syerston Scandium Project in New South Wales, designed to produce ~60 tonnes of scandium a year for aerospace-grade aluminum alloys. The US Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital signed a conditional commitment of up to US$400M in long-term debt for the project; the company is also pursuing a US listing.

nodes.label: GlobalFoundries
nodes.description: US-headquartered contract semiconductor manufacturer (NASDAQ: GFS) with fabs in Malta NY, Burlington VT, Dresden and Singapore, serving automotive, IoT and data center markets. Signed a letter of intent with the US Commerce Department for a $300M CHIPS R&D award to develop silicon photonics and co-packaged optics (its SCALE platform) for AI data centers.

nodes.label: Genesis Mission first project cohort (278 projects)
nodes.id: target:Genesis Mission first project cohort (278 projects)
nodes.description: First cohort of 278 projects selected under the Genesis Mission, the U.S. Department of Energy's AI-for-science initiative — 87 led by DOE/NNSA national labs, 168 by universities and 19 by companies, spanning nuclear energy, fusion, critical minerals and intelligent chip design. DOE called it the largest response to a funding opportunity in its history.

nodes.label: Kepler Computing
nodes.description: Moraga, California semiconductor startup developing a new class of AI memory using 3D-stacked ferroelectric technology that puts compute logic directly adjacent to weight storage, targeting the memory bottleneck in AI accelerators. Selected by the Commerce Department in July 2026 for up to $245M in CHIPS Act R&D incentives (letter of intent), the second-largest of seven awards.

nodes.label: Norm Ai
nodes.description: New York legal-AI company building regulatory and legal AI agents, plus an AI-native law firm (Norm Law) where human attorneys supervise its agents on outcome-based pricing; raised a $120M Series C led by Khosla Ventures at a $1.2B valuation in July 2026, with Blackstone, Bain Capital Ventures and Coatue participating.

nodes.label: Senra Systems
nodes.description: California aerospace/defense manufacturer (founded 2023 by ex-SpaceX engineers Jordan Black and Benjamin Shanahan) automating wire-harness production with its Amp software platform. Raised a $65M Series B co-led by Lowercarbon Capital and Interlagos — with Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz and Founders Fund participating — to open a third factory; total funding tops $112M.

nodes.label: Glow
nodes.description: AI-era endpoint-security company founded by Roi Tiger (CEO, ex-Meta), Omer Singer (CTO, ex-Snowflake cybersecurity strategy) and Ophir Arie (ex-Claroty), rethinking endpoint protection for enterprises where employees and autonomous AI agents both operate on the network. Emerged from stealth July 2026 with $180M at a $1.2B valuation, led by Sequoia, Cyberstarts, Greenoaks and Redpoint.

nodes.label: HappyRobot
nodes.description: Enterprise AI company whose platform deploys autonomous agents to automate workflows in logistics, supply chain, insurance, energy and financial services; customers include DHL, Kuehne + Nagel, Naturgy and Uber. Raised a $150M Series C in August 2026 at a $1.2B post-money valuation, led by Prysm Capital and co-led by Eurazeo (a16z is an earlier backer), bringing total funding to ~$200M.

nodes.label: Niron Magnetics
nodes.description: Minneapolis-area company commercializing rare-earth-free Iron Nitride permanent magnets, based on technology developed at the University of Minnesota. The US Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital signed a conditional 20-year loan commitment of up to $150M to fund its 287,000 sq ft Sartell, Minnesota plant, slated to produce up to 1,500 tons of magnets annually from 2027.

nodes.label: Multibeam Corporation
nodes.description: Santa Clara semiconductor-equipment maker founded in 2010 and led by David K. Lam (Lam Research's founding CEO), building multi-column e-beam lithography systems for advanced packaging, chip-ID security and photonics. Received a $140M letter of intent under the CHIPS R&D program in July 2026 for advanced packaging technology to assemble and stack multiple chips.

nodes.label: State Affairs
nodes.description: AI-powered policy and regulatory intelligence platform combining a newsroom covering all 50 states and the federal government with structured legislative data; used by a third of state and federal elected officials plus enterprises like Walmart and Mastercard. Co-founded by CEO Evan Burns; announced $70M in total funding (July 2026) from Founders Fund, Khosla Ventures, Tru Arrow and others.

nodes.label: Greenoaks Prime Radiant Founders Offshore LP
nodes.id: target:Greenoaks Prime Radiant Founders Offshore LP
nodes.description: The offshore sleeve of Greenoaks' code-named 'Prime Radiant' deal vehicle, renamed from 'Greenoaks Generations Founders Offshore LP' per its amended Form D, which reports $115.5M raised from 4 investors (first sale June 26, 2026). Runs parallel to the $576.5M onshore Greenoaks Prime Radiant Founders LP; the underlying deal target is undisclosed.

nodes.label: Flourish
nodes.description: AI research company (founded 2025 by ex-Amazon S-team executive Rob Williams and CTRL-Labs founder/neuroscientist Thomas Reardon) hunting for the brain's 'core algorithm' to build brain-inspired, energy-efficient, continuously learning AI ('Cortex AI'). Closed a $500M round at a $2.5B valuation with Jeff Bezos contributing close to $100M, alongside GV, Lux Capital and Catalio.

nodes.label: Neo Security
nodes.description: "Agentic Software Control" security company founded by SentinelOne, Wiz and Palo Alto Networks veterans, giving SecOps teams inventory, posture and policy control over AI agents, AI-enabled apps, browsers and identities; emerged from stealth in July 2026 with $100M from Andreessen Horowitz and Bessemer, plus Craft and Merlin Ventures.

nodes.label: Strategic Bauxite USA, LLC (SBX)
nodes.description: US critical-minerals venture receiving an $85.5M equity investment from the Department of War's IBAS program (plus $64.5M private co-investment) to build a vertically integrated US supply chain for refractory-grade bauxite — currently import-dependent on China. Funds go in part to acquiring and expanding the First Bauxite mine in Guyana, targeting 100% of US military demand.

nodes.label: Standard Bauxite
nodes.description: Refractory-grade bauxite supplier named 'Standard Bauxite' in the White House fact sheet; the Department of War release identifies the counterparty as Strategic Bauxite USA, LLC (SBX), which acquired Canada's First Bauxite Corporation. The DoW's $85.5M IBAS equity investment (plus $64.5M private co-investment) funds expansion of the First Bauxite mine in Guyana, calcination facilities, and a US brown-fused alumina plant.

nodes.label: Singularity Defense
nodes.description: Los Angeles defense startup (founded by Jack Oswald and Shail Giroux) building low-cost missile/drone interceptors, with a manufacturing team drawn from Tesla and Toyota applying automotive assembly-line methods to scale production. Emerged from two years in stealth in July 2026 with an $80M Series A at a $400M valuation, co-led by Khosla Ventures and Felicis, with NEA, Menlo Ventures, Y Combinator and others participating.

nodes.label: Extropic
nodes.description: AI hardware startup founded by Guillaume Verdon building thermodynamic sampling units (TSUs) — probabilistic chips that use natural thermal fluctuations to run simulation, optimization and AI workloads at a fraction of conventional computing's energy cost. Received a Commerce Department letter of intent for up to $75M under the CHIPS program in July 2026.

nodes.label: Khosla Ventures MM SPV, LLC
nodes.description: Delaware special-purpose vehicle formed by Khosla Ventures in 2026 (Vinod Khosla, Samir Kaul and Sven Strohband listed as managing directors), which raised $60.5M per an August 2026 Form D. The underlying portfolio company ('MM') is not disclosed in the filing; the vehicle is structured as a venture capital fund.

nodes.label: Prometheus project (Idaho National Laboratory and partners)
nodes.id: target:Prometheus project (Idaho National Laboratory and partners)
nodes.description: A DOE Genesis Mission initiative led by Idaho National Laboratory with a 32-partner consortium (Oak Ridge, Argonne, Sandia, plus X-energy, TerraPower, Oklo, NVIDIA and AWS among 20+ industry partners) using AI to design, license, build and operate nuclear reactors — targeting 2x schedule compression and >50% cost reduction. Awarded a $60M three-year Phase II grant in July 2026, the largest single Genesis Mission award, with $200M+ in industry cost share.

nodes.label: Convex
nodes.description: All-in-one TypeScript backend platform (database, functions, real-time sync, workflow) founded in 2021 by ex-Dropbox infrastructure engineers, now positioned as the reliable backend for AI-agent-written software; raised a $57M Series B led by Insight Partners with a16z, Spark Capital and Justin Kan participating, bringing total funding to $110.5M.

nodes.label: P-1 AI
nodes.description: San Mateo-based engineering-AI startup co-founded by former Airbus CTO Paul Eremenko, building 'Archie', an agentic AI mechanical/electrical engineer for industrial teams in data-center, automotive and aerospace & defense design. Announced a $50M Series A led by NEA in July 2026 (Jeff Immelt joining the board), following a $23M seed led by Radical Ventures in 2025.

nodes.label: Thintronics
nodes.description: Semiconductor materials company developing ultra-low-loss inter-layer dielectrics (ILD) for next-generation chip interconnects and advanced packaging — a market where ~98% of advanced substrate ILD supply comes from one foreign company. Received a Commerce Department letter of intent for up to $50M under the CHIPS R&D program's $874M July 2026 announcement, with Commerce taking a minority equity stake as a condition.

nodes.label: Altimeter Himalaya Fund I, L.P.
nodes.description: Boston-based venture capital fund vehicle from Brad Gerstner's Altimeter Capital; its July 2026 Form D reports $40M raised and fully subscribed (first sale June 29, 2026), with Gerstner, Matthew Tolve and John Kiernan III as related persons. No public announcement found — the 'Himalaya' vehicle's specific strategy is undisclosed.

nodes.label: OBSIDIA Semiconductors
nodes.description: San Francisco hardware-security company building non-invasive counterfeit and malicious-component detection for AI and defense chip supply chains; its ReelScan platform uses RF fingerprinting to authenticate ICs on component reels. Received a $34M letter of intent under the CHIPS R&D program in July 2026.

nodes.label: Aeluma
nodes.description: Nasdaq-listed semiconductor company (ALMU) in Goleta, California developing photonic and electronic chips on large-diameter substrates for AI interconnects, mobile, defense and quantum; signed a CHIPS R&D Office letter of intent with the Commerce Department in July 2026 for up to $30M to develop indium-phosphide-free photodetector and laser technology.

nodes.label: Ambrook
nodes.description: Financial-management software startup ('QuickBooks for the real economy') founded in 2020 by Mackenzie Burnett, Dan Schlosser and Jeff Anders — bookkeeping, payments and cash management for farms, ranches, trucking, construction and property businesses, now 8,000+ customers. Raised a $30M Series B in August 2026 led by Lachy Groom with Thrive Capital and Thomson Reuters Ventures participating, bringing total funding to $59M.

nodes.label: Ellis
nodes.description: AI-native operations platform for private credit from Cadre co-founder Ryan Williams, using AI agents to automate credit managers' reconciliation, LP reporting, SBIC compliance and document workflows. Emerged from stealth July 2026 with $10M+ seed led by First Round Capital, with Khosla Ventures, 645 Ventures, Harlem Capital and Slow Ventures participating.

nodes.label: Summit Ridge Energy
nodes.description: Leading US commercial and community solar operator founded in 2017, which develops, owns and operates 275+ distributed solar and storage facilities (3+ GW) across the Midwest, Mid-Atlantic and New England, having raised over $7B in project capital. BlackRock's Global Infrastructure Partners agreed in July 2026 to acquire a majority, controlling interest.

nodes.label: Kirkwood Infrastructure Group
nodes.description: Fiber-infrastructure developer launched July 2026 as a wholly owned venture of funds managed by Blue Owl's Digital Infrastructure strategy, building conduit and high-count fiber networks connecting hyperscale data centers across the US. Led by CEO Scott Bergs; launched with the integration of Florida's South Reach Networks (400 miles of network, 40 data centers) plus 200+ miles under construction in Louisiana and Mississippi.

nodes.label: Nippon Gateway Infrastructure (NGI)
nodes.description: Enterprise-focused colocation data center platform in Japan, formed July 2026 by DigitalBridge and Japan Extensive Infrastructure (JEXI). Launched with data center assets acquired from NEC in Greater Tokyo and Greater Osaka (NEC remains a key customer), led by CEO Hiroshi Ogasawara, with plans to expand through acquisitions and new development across Japan's major markets.

nodes.label: SB Neo
nodes.description: US neocloud company established July 2026 by SoftBank Corp. (51%) and SoftBank Group (49%) to rent GPU cloud capacity to American enterprises and hyperscalers from fiscal 2027, scaling toward 10GW of AI data-center capacity and building on SoftBank's Japanese GPU cloud and Infrinia AI Cloud OS stack.

nodes.label: Proxima Fusion
nodes.description: Munich-based stellarator fusion company, the first spinout of the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, building on the Wendelstein 7-X program toward its Stellaris commercial fusion plant. Raised EUR 411M ($468M) in July 2026 at a EUR 2.4B valuation, led by XTX Ventures and East X Ventures with Google and RWE as strategic investors — Europe's best-funded fusion company.

nodes.label: Mistral AI
nodes.description: Paris-based frontier AI lab known for high-performance open-weight models and its Le Chat assistant, positioned as Europe's leading independent AI company. In July 2026 Microsoft announced an expanded strategic partnership described as a multibillion-dollar commitment, covering European GPU capacity, Mistral models in Microsoft Foundry/Copilot Studio, and sovereign deployments for regulated industries.

nodes.label: Volta Infra Holdings
nodes.description: AI-cloud financing startup ('the utility of compute') founded in 2026 by ex-Brookfield infrastructure executives Ricard Boada and Sofia Gumuzio, arranging capital alongside GPU capacity so AI labs can afford NVIDIA hardware. Raised $300M at a $2.4B valuation led by a16z and Altimeter, with NVIDIA and Michael Dell backing plus $5B financing via Azora; ~1 GW of power secured and a $10B six-year compute contract signed.

nodes.label: Generalist AI
nodes.description: San Francisco robotics-AI company founded in 2024 by ex-DeepMind researchers Pete Florence and Andy Zeng with Andrew Barry (ex-Boston Dynamics), building general-purpose 'robot brain' models (GEN-1, April 2026) trained on data from its robot-training gloves. Raised $400M in June 2026 at a $2B valuation led by Radical Ventures, with NVIDIA and Bezos Expeditions among returning backers; total funding exceeds $500M.

nodes.label: France sovereign AI infrastructure framework
nodes.description: Brookfield's AI infrastructure framework agreement with the French government, announced at the February 2025 Paris AI Action Summit at €20B and expanded to €30B (confirmed in Brookfield's Q2 2026 results) to enable French sovereign AI infrastructure — mostly data centers built and operated by Brookfield portfolio company Data4, including campuses at E-Valley Cambrai and Escaudain in Hauts-de-France, plus power and network investments.

nodes.label: Andreessen Horowitz Fund X-B - AI Infrastructure, L.P.
nodes.id: target:Andreessen Horowitz Fund X-B - AI Infrastructure, L.P.
nodes.description: Delaware venture fund vehicle in a16z's Fund X family dedicated to AI infrastructure, per a July 2026 Form D (indefinite offering; Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz as principals). Part of a16z's ~$3B AI-infrastructure strategy within its $15B early-2026 raise, backing systems that help technical teams build, secure and deploy AI.

nodes.label: Andreessen Horowitz Fund X-B - AI Applications, L.P.
nodes.id: target:Andreessen Horowitz Fund X-B - AI Applications, L.P.
nodes.description: A newly registered Andreessen Horowitz venture fund vehicle dedicated to AI applications — the 'X-B' sleeve of a16z's Fund X family and successor to Fund IX - AI Applications. Its initial Form D (filed July 16, 2026) reports an indefinite offering with no sales yet, signaling a16z is raising its next AI applications fund; fund size is undisclosed.

nodes.label: Andreessen Horowitz LSV Fund V-B, L.P.
nodes.id: target:Andreessen Horowitz LSV Fund V-B, L.P.
nodes.description: Parallel vehicle of Andreessen Horowitz's fifth late-stage venture fund (LSV Fund V), the a16z strategy that backs growth-stage technology companies; the LSV series began with a $2B fund in 2019. Its July 2026 Form D (Menlo Park; Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz as related persons) reports an indefinite offering amount with no sales yet at filing.

nodes.label: Altimeter Kilauea Fund II, L.P.
nodes.description: Delaware venture-capital vehicle formed in 2026 by Brad Gerstner's Altimeter Capital (Boston), which filed a Form D on 2026-07-28 for a $40M offering ($2M minimum, no sales yet at filing). The specific underlying investment behind the "Kilauea" vehicle is not disclosed in the filing.

nodes.label: Cathedral
nodes.description: Stealth military-cybersecurity startup founded by four DOGE alumni (Gavin Kliger — former Pentagon chief data officer — Luke Farritor, Marko Elez, Jack Stein), building AI-driven offensive and defensive cyber tools it aims to sell to the US government. Raised $160M in July 2026 at a $1.4B valuation, co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia, both taking board seats; no disclosed revenue or contracts yet.

nodes.label: Prentis
nodes.description: AI research lab founded in April 2026 by Ritankar Das (CEO) with Reid Hoffman and Mark Pincus as co-founders, training computer-use models (its Hive-32B) that automate office workflows like insurance claims processing. Reported in talks to raise $100M at a ~$1B valuation, with up to $50M in signed customer contracts and 25+ hires from OpenAI, DeepMind and Meta.

nodes.label: GPx TX LP
nodes.description: Delaware limited partnership formed in 2026 by GPx, the venture firm of ex-Founders Fund GP Brian Singerman and Quiet Capital's Lee Linden (backed by Peter Thiel); the July 2026 Form D lists an indefinite offering with no sales yet. The 'TX' vehicle's specific purpose is undisclosed — GPx's model backs emerging seed managers and leads later-stage rounds in their breakout companies.

nodes.label: Quiet Select TX LP
nodes.description: New pooled investment vehicle from San Francisco-based Quiet Capital (Form D filed July 28, 2026; GP: Quiet Select TX GP LLC), with Quiet Capital founder Lee Linden and former Founders Fund partner Brian Singerman listed as related persons. Indefinite offering size with no sales at filing; the 'Select' naming pattern suggests a deal-specific co-invest vehicle, but the underlying target is not disclosed in the filing.

nodes.label: Craft Ventures V, LP
nodes.description: Fifth flagship early-stage venture fund of Craft Ventures, the San Francisco B2B SaaS-focused firm co-founded by David Sacks (PayPal founding COO, Yammer founder, and until March 2026 White House AI and crypto czar). Delaware LP formed 2026; Form D filed August 7, 2026 with an indefinite offering amount and first sale yet to occur, with Sacks listed as managing member of the general partner.

nodes.label: LifeMine Therapeutics
nodes.description: Clinical-stage biotech (Cambridge, MA; founded by Greg Verdine) that mines fungal genomes for drug candidates via its "Top-Down Drug Discovery" platform; raised $263M (a $188M Series E plus $75M Series D) in August 2026 from Bezos Expeditions, Gates Frontier and RA Capital to advance LIFE-001, a novel calcineurin-activation inhibitor for preventing organ-transplant rejection.

nodes.label: CuspAI
nodes.description: Cambridge (UK)-based AI-for-materials-discovery company whose generative search engine predicts viable molecular and chemical structures, used by ASML, Meta, Samsung and Hyundai; raised a $450M Series B at a $2.6B valuation in July 2026 led by Kleiner Perkins and NEA, with Bezos Expeditions among new investors — up from a $520M valuation nine months earlier.

nodes.label: General Intuition
nodes.description: AI research lab spun out of gaming clip platform Medal, training world models and agents for spatial-temporal reasoning on hundreds of millions of hours of gameplay footage with embedded controller-action labels; led by CEO Pim de Witte. Raised $320M at a $2.3B valuation in June 2026, led by Khosla Ventures with Jeff Bezos, Eric Schmidt and General Catalyst participating.

nodes.label: Monogram
nodes.description: AI interface startup from Udemy and Carbon Health founder Eren Bali (with Edouard Tabet and Murat Akbal) that answers queries with generated visual, interactive interfaces instead of chat text; launched from stealth July 2026 with an iOS app and a $40M seed led by DST Global and Lux Capital, with angels including Garry Tan and Arthur Mensch.

nodes.label: Odyssey
nodes.description: AI lab founded in 2023 by autonomous-vehicle veterans Oliver Cameron (ex-Voyage/Cruise) and Jeff Hawke (ex-Wayve), building general-purpose 'world models' — causal, multimodal simulations of the physical world for gaming, robotics and interactive video. Raised a $310M Series B in June 2026 at a $1.45B valuation led by Natural Capital, with Amazon, AMD Ventures, GV and angels including Elad Gil and Garry Tan.

nodes.label: SkillBench
nodes.description: Santa Barbara startup (formerly Tacitly, Inc.) building AI-enabled workforce skill measurement and optimization for enterprises adopting generative AI; co-founded by researchers Matt Beane (UCSB) and Juho Kim (KAIST), with Reid Hoffman on the board per its August 2026 Form D, which reports ~$15.1M sold of a ~$17.1M offering.

nodes.label: Prometheus
nodes.description: Physical-AI company (Project Prometheus) co-founded and co-led by Jeff Bezos and former Verily co-founder Vik Bajaj, building an 'artificial general engineer' to automate design and manufacturing of complex physical systems — jet engines to drug compounds. Launched late 2025 with $6.2B and raised a further $12B at a $41B valuation in mid-2026.

nodes.label: Panthalassa
nodes.description: Portland, Oregon company (founded 2016) building autonomous wave-powered floating platforms that generate ocean energy and run onboard AI inference compute with seawater cooling; raised a $140M Series B led by Peter Thiel at a reported ~$1B valuation to build its Oregon pilot plant for Ocean-3 series nodes, with commercial systems planned for 2027.

nodes.label: Radical Numerics
nodes.description: San Francisco AI research lab building 'general biological intelligence' — models that read, write and design across DNA, RNA and proteins — founded by Eric Nguyen, Michael Poli, Stefano Massaroli and Armin Thomas (Stanford / Liquid AI alumni). Launched June 2026 with a $50M seed led by Emergence Capital, following pre-seed backing involving Patrick Collison; previewing its Omnii genomic language model.

nodes.label: Brookfield Middle East Partners (BMEP)
nodes.description: Brookfield's Middle East private-equity fund, which held a ~$2B first close in July 2026 with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund as strategic anchor and Brookfield committing $500M. Targets buyouts and minority growth-equity deals in financial services, industrials, technology and healthcare across GCC markets, with 50% of investments earmarked for Saudi Arabia.

nodes.label: Paducah AI/HPC innovation campus
nodes.description: Planned AI/HPC campus redeveloping parts of the DOE's Paducah Site (a Cold War uranium-enrichment facility) in western Kentucky under DOE's American Energy Hubs initiative: over $100B in expected private investment, ~8,000 construction jobs. Brookfield develops and operates the 1.8GW-capacity campus; NextEra builds up to 2GW of gas generation and 2.6GW of battery storage adjacent, with full build-out targeted for the early 2030s.

nodes.label: Savannah River Site AI data center
nodes.id: target:Savannah River Site AI data center
nodes.description: A planned 1 GW AI data center with ~2 GW of dedicated on-site generation (natural gas transitioning to nuclear) on federal land at the DOE/NNSA Savannah River Site in South Carolina. NNSA selected site operator Amentum in July 2026 to negotiate a phased land-lease public-private partnership; no lease award is final yet and no dollar figures have been disclosed.

nodes.label: Kuwait Oil Company Pipeline JV (Project Peregrine)
nodes.id: target:Kuwait Oil Company Pipeline JV (Project Peregrine)
nodes.description: A $16.0B lease-and-leaseback joint venture over Kuwait Oil Company's entire domestic and export crude pipeline network (13 pipelines, ~320 km). A Blackstone/Brookfield/KKR consortium holds 49% (equal shares) with KOC keeping 51%, ownership and operations; the JV leases usage rights back to KOC for 20.5 years for a volume-based tariff, generating ~$7.85B upfront — Kuwait's largest-ever FDI.

nodes.label: TotalEnergies European renewables portfolio (Germany/Spain/France/Poland)
nodes.description: A 1.2 GW portfolio of developed solar and onshore-wind assets across Germany, Spain, France and Poland, with an enterprise value of ~€1.8B. KKR (through an insurance account it manages) agreed to acquire a 50% stake; TotalEnergies retains the other 50% and continues operating the assets, part of its farm-down capital-recycling model.

nodes.label: Discovery Loop
nodes.description: Public benefit corporation founded in August 2026 by Google veterans Jeff Dean (CEO), Sanjay Ghemawat, Oriol Vinyals and Quoc Le to use AI to automate large-scale scientific and engineering experimentation. Seed round co-led by Radical Ventures and Khosla Ventures, with Alphabet participating as founding investor and cloud partner alongside Lightspeed and Kleiner Perkins.

nodes.label: Prime Intellect
nodes.description: AI infrastructure company (founded 2024, CEO Vincent Weisser) building an open 'superintelligence stack' — GPU compute, reinforcement-learning frameworks and evals that let enterprises train and run their own AI models and agents instead of relying on frontier labs. Raised a $130M Series A at a $1B valuation led by Radical Ventures, with NVIDIA Ventures, Intel Capital and Dell Technologies Capital; ~$100M revenue run rate.

nodes.label: Moove
nodes.description: Mobility-infrastructure company founded 2020 by Ladi Delano and Jide Odunsi (now UAE-headquartered) that finances, owns and operates vehicle fleets — ~42,000 vehicles across 29 cities — and runs autonomous-fleet operations, including as a fleet operator for Waymo in Phoenix and Miami. Raised a $250M Series C led by Mubadala at a $2.1B valuation, with Woven Capital (Toyota) and Uber among backers.

nodes.label: MOZN
nodes.description: Riyadh-based enterprise AI company focused on financial-crime prevention and decision intelligence; its FOCAL platform (AML/KYC) serves 150+ financial-services and public-sector customers across the Middle East. Received a strategic investment from HUMAIN (Saudi PIF's AI company) — HUMAIN Ventures' first investment in a Saudi company — paired with a partnership to co-build enterprise AI solutions.
